newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi welcomes Feb preliminary CPI.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi welcomes Feb preliminary CPI.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi welcomed preliminary CPI data from six sample cities on Thursday, saying they showed that Italy was succeeding in cleaning up its finances for EMU and it would be "unpardonable" to stop now.
The data pointed to a year-on-year inflation rate of 2.3 percent and a flat monthly rate.
"Initial data for February...if confirmed, would represent a further positive step in the government's economic and monetary policy," Prodi said in a statement.

"Italy is moving forward on the road to cleaning up its public finances with a healthy, non-inflationary policy which is pushing us with determination towards the difficult goal of monetary union," he said.
"Today's data show that to stop now would be an unpardonable error."
Five further sample cities publish preliminary February data on Friday and national statistics institute ISTAT publishes the final inflation figures on March 4.
